The main takeaway from our work is that

for a genetic association study, if one is willing to make a reasonable assumption that the underlying genetic model lies within a range of models, one can use the maximum over the range of Cochran-Armitage trend tests, which is easy to compute and is very robust to model misspecification.
the p values calculated using simulated permutations are only valid asymptotically, and may be very inaccurate for small sample sizes.
